assistant_message.content: Great request! I'll create a detailed step-by-step instructional PDF on how to build data analytic overlays with API-sourced data. Let me plan this out and put together a comprehensive guide for you.
I've completed the research and drafted the guide. Now I'm expanding it into a fully detailed, polished instructional document with code examples and converting it to PDF.

Your step-by-step instructional PDF is ready! Here is a summary of everything covered in the guide:

**Building Data Analytic Overlays with API-Sourced Data** is a comprehensive 15-section guide that walks through the entire process from start to finish:

| Section | What You'll Learn |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Architecture Overview** | How the API, pipeline, and visualization layers connect |
| **Step 1 — API Selection** | How to evaluate and choose the right API with a checklist |
| **Step 2 — Dev Environment** | Setting up Python, project structure, and securing credentials |
| **Step 3 — Authentication** | OAuth 2.0, API Keys, and Bearer Tokens with full code examples |
| **Step 4 — Fetching Data** | Handling pagination, rate limits, and exponential backoff retries |
| **Step 5 — Data Cleaning** | Parsing JSON, flattening nested structures, and schema validation |
| **Step 6 — Library Selection** | Decision guide for Python (Folium, Plotly, Bokeh) and JavaScript (Leaflet.js, D3.js) |
| **Step 7 — Building the Overlay** | Full code for a geographic heatmap and a trend-line chart overlay |
| **Step 8 — Automation** | Scheduling pipelines with Python `schedule` and Celery |
| **Step 9 — Deployment** | Serving via Flask, embedding in dashboards, and deployment options |
| **Step 10 — Monitoring** | Logging, failure alerts, and a maintenance checklist |
| **Real-World Example** | Complete end-to-end air quality heatmap using the Open-Meteo API |
| **Best Practices** | Common pitfalls and how to avoid them |

The PDF includes all code snippets, comparison tables, and references to authoritative sources. Feel free to share it directly with your friends!
